claim: `isMulCommutative_mono` is misnamed. It proves `s ≤ t → IsMulCommutative t → IsMulCommutative s`, so commutativity passes from the larger subobject down to the smaller one. As a function of the subobject, `IsMulCommutative` is antitone, not monotone. Mathlib's `_mono`/`_anti` convention, and the sibling lemmas for predicates inherited by smaller objects (`Set.Subsingleton.anti`, `SimpleGraph.IsAcyclic.anti`, `SimpleGraph.CliqueFree.anti`, `Graph.Loopless.anti`, `Graph.Simple.anti`, `ConvexCone.Salient.anti`, `ConvexCone.Blunt.anti`, `Filter.Subsingleton.anti`, versus `ConvexCone.Pointed.mono` for the upward direction), call this `_anti`. The PR's own title already announces `isMulCommutative_anti`, so the code and the title disagree. The generated additive name `isAddCommutative_mono` has the same problem.
requested_change: Rename `isMulCommutative_mono` to `isMulCommutative_anti`, which through `to_additive` also renames `isAddCommutative_mono` to `isAddCommutative_anti`. Keep the statement, docstrings and proof unchanged.
evidence: Read the lemma at Defs.lean:350-356; its hypothesis is `h : s ≤ t` with `[IsMulCommutative t]`, and its conclusion is `IsMulCommutative s`. `declaration_search isMulCommutative_anti` found nothing in the base or the PR, so the name is free. A `content_search` for lemmas named `*.anti`/`*_anti` (a sample of 40 files) found the `.anti` naming for inheritance by smaller objects listed in the claim, and `Pointed.mono` next to `Blunt.anti`/`Salient.anti` in Geometry/Convex/Cone/Basic.lean for the opposite direction. `naming_norm` returned subject_unresolved (unmeasured). `lean_verify_edit` (line mode, lines 350-356) replaced the lemma with the same body under the name `isMulCommutative_anti`, followed by `#check @isAddCommutative_anti`. It reported success, with no errors or warnings, and the info showed `@isAddCommutative_anti : ... s ≤ t → ∀ [IsAddCommutative ↥t], IsAddCommutative ↥s`.
